variants.name: Whiteboard & Marker
variants.generalStyle: Clean white background (#FAFAFA) with a faint dry-erase grid texture (light gray lines at ~0.06 opacity, 40px spacing). All decorative DSA illustrations rendered in a hand-drawn marker style using SVG paths with slightly imperfect strokes (stroke-linecap: round, stroke-width: 2-3px, subtle wobble via SVG filter feTurbulence at low intensity). Primary ink colors: blue marker (#2563EB), red marker (#DC2626), green marker (#16A34A), black marker (#1E293B). Typography: Caveat 600-700 for headings (handwritten feel), Inter 400-500 for body text (readable). Cards have a white surface with light gray dashed borders (border: 2px dashed #CBD5E1) resembling taped-up index cards. Hover states add a subtle yellow highlighter wash (rgba(250,204,21,0.15)). Drop shadows are soft and minimal (0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)). Spacing is generous. Small doodle accents (arrows, underlines, circles) scattered as decorative SVGs.

landingPageStyles.flow: The page reads like a professor walking you through a whiteboard session. Each scroll section is a 'lesson' building on the last — no traditional hero/features/CTA grid.

sections.name: The Problem (Chapter 1)
sections.description: Opens with a hand-drawn 'problem statement' on the whiteboard: 'You want to work at a top tech company. But where do you start?' Drawn as a question mark inside a binary tree node. Below: hand-drawn arrows branch out to 3 pain points (scattered resources, no structure, no feedback) each sketched as a dead-end node with an X. Marker doodles animate in as you scroll (SVG stroke-dashoffset reveal). Company logos drawn inside a hashmap visualization: { 'dream': [Google, Meta, Amazon...] }. No traditional CTA button yet — just the problem marinating.

sections.name: The Solution (Chapter 2) — Interactive Demo
sections.description: Whiteboard 'erases' (fade transition) and redraws with the solution. Three feature panels appear as hand-drawn index cards pinned to the board: (1) INTERACTIVE WALKTHROUGHS — a live mini-demo of the step-by-step algorithm visualizer embedded inline. Shows a hand-drawn array [1,2,3,3] with a pointer sliding across, 'SEEN' hashset building up, step counter '2/13'. User can click play/pause. Drawn as a whiteboard diagram that actually works. (2) VIDEO SOLUTIONS — embedded video thumbnail with a hand-drawn play button triangle, course filmstrip showing chapter structure (Arrays → Trees → Graphs), duration pills in marker. (3) NEETBOT AI — a mock chat interface drawn as speech bubbles on the whiteboard. Shows: User bubble 'Im stuck on two sum' → NeetBot bubble 'Think about what data structure lets you check if a complement exists in O(1)...' with a blinking cursor. Chat bubbles have dashed borders and slight rotation like sticky notes.

sections.name: The Proof (Chapter 3) — Social Proof + CTA
sections.description: Board fills with 'results': testimonials drawn as sticky notes pinned to the whiteboard with slight rotations (-1 to 2deg). Each has a hand-drawn checkmark and the company name circled. Stats drawn as a bar chart — tall green bars for '1M+ engineers', '1000+ problems'. Below: a hand-drawn flowchart showing the user journey: Start → Pick a Plan → Study → Get Hired, each step a circled node with marker arrows. The final node 'Get Hired' has a starburst around it. CTA is a large hand-drawn 'START HERE →' with a circled button. Founder section is a small margin note in the corner: a hand-drawn portrait circle with 'Hi, Im Navi' in Caveat and a brief bio as a handwritten paragraph.

landingPageStyles.animations: SVG stroke-dashoffset drawing animations on scroll. Each section's illustrations draw themselves as user scrolls into view. Sticky notes appear with a slight 'pin drop' animation (scale from 0.9 to 1 + subtle rotation). No smooth scrolling — each chapter snaps into view. Interactive demo elements (walkthrough, chat) are functional but styled as whiteboard drawings.
landingPageStyles.uniqueElement: The interactive algorithm walkthrough is LIVE on the landing page — not just a screenshot. Users can step through a real 'Contains Duplicate' solution right on the whiteboard, experiencing the product before signing up.

variants.name: Retro-Futurism / Cyberpunk
variants.generalStyle: Deep void background (#0A0A0F) with neon accent colors, monospace-influenced typography. Headings: JetBrains Mono 600-700 or Orbitron 700. Body: IBM Plex Sans 400. Subtle CRT scanline overlay (repeating-linear-gradient at 2px intervals, very low opacity). Neon glow effects (text-shadow: 0 0 8px accent, box-shadow: 0 0 12px accent). Sharp corners (border-radius: 2-4px max). Borders: 1px solid with neon tint. Glitch micro-animation on hero text. Terminal/HUD aesthetic.

landingPageStyles.flow: The entire page IS a terminal. Users 'navigate' by scrolling, but the content renders as if it's terminal output being streamed. Each section types itself out. The page tells you about NeetCode as if you just ran '$ neetcode --help'. This is NOT a traditional landing page — it's a product experience.

sections.name: Boot Sequence (Hero)
sections.description: Page opens with a terminal boot sequence animation: '> Initializing NeetCode v4.2.0...', '> Loading 1,247 problems...', '> Connecting to NeetBot AI...', '> Ready.' typed out character by character with green text on black. Then the main prompt appears: '$ neetcode --about' which 'outputs' the value proposition in formatted terminal text. Stats appear as a system status readout: 'ENGINEERS_SERVED=1000000+', 'PROBLEMS_AVAILABLE=1000+', 'VIDEO_SOLUTIONS=1000+'. Company logos appear as ASCII art or monospace text in a bordered box: '[ TRUSTED BY: Google | Meta | Amazon | Microsoft | Netflix | OpenAI ]'.

sections.name: Feature Showcase (Interactive Terminal)
sections.description: Three tabbed terminal windows side by side (each with title bar dots and neon-bordered frame). TAB 1 — '$ neetcode solve contains-duplicate': Shows a LIVE interactive walkthrough in terminal style. The array renders as monospace text: 'nums = [1, 2, 3, 3]'. A pointer indicator '      ^' moves through. Hash set state prints line by line: 'seen = {1}', 'seen = {1, 2}', etc. Step controls are terminal commands: '[n]ext [p]rev [r]eset'. Fully interactive — user presses n to advance. TAB 2 — '$ neetcode watch arrays': Video player embedded in a terminal frame. Playlist sidebar shows course chapters as numbered terminal lines: '01 RAM (6 min) [FREE]', '02 Static Arrays (15 min)', etc. Video thumbnail has a green-bordered play button. TAB 3 — '$ neetcode ask "how to approach two sum"': NeetBot AI chat in terminal format. Shows: '> how to approach two sum?', then NeetBot response streams character by character: 'Consider using a hash map to store complements...'. Blinking cursor at bottom. User can type a pre-set question to trigger a demo response.

sections.name: Social Proof (Logs Output)
sections.description: Section header: '$ neetcode --testimonials | head -5'. Testimonials render as 'log entries': '[2024-03-15] amog@google.com: "Signed my offer at Google L4..."', each with a timestamp, user handle, and quote. Green checkmark prefixes. Company icons as small neon-tinted badges.

sections.name: Courses (Directory Listing)
sections.description: '$ ls -la /courses/' renders a directory listing: 'drwxr-xr-x  dsa-beginners/    25hrs  MEDIUM', 'drwxr-xr-x  advanced-algo/    25hrs  HARD', etc. Each line is clickable and expands to show course details. Difficulty colors: green/yellow/red text. Course thumbnails appear as small ASCII-art previews on hover.

sections.name: CTA (Install Command)
sections.description: '$ neetcode install --plan free' styled as an npm/pip install output with a progress bar: '████████░░░░ 67%  Installing NeetCode 150...'. Below: two CTA 'commands': '$ neetcode start --free' (green bordered) and '$ neetcode upgrade --pro' (cyan bordered with neon glow). Founder appears as '$ man neetcode' manual page output with NAME, DESCRIPTION, AUTHOR sections.

landingPageStyles.animations: Typewriter character-by-character text reveal (40-60ms per character). Terminal cursor blink (CSS animation, 1s interval). Glitch effect on hero brand name (translateX ±2px, 0.1s, occasional). CRT scanline overlay (repeating-linear-gradient). Tab switching has an instant terminal-style flip (no smooth transition). Interactive elements respond with terminal 'output' animations. Subtle neon pulse on active elements.
landingPageStyles.uniqueElement: The interactive algorithm walkthrough runs in a real terminal-style interface. Users type 'n' or click [next] to step through the algorithm. The NeetBot AI chat accepts typed input and streams a pre-scripted response character by character. The whole page feels like you're using the product already.

variants.name: DSA Visual
variants.generalStyle: Dark slate background (#0D1117, GitHub-dark inspired) with interactive data structure visualizations woven into the design. SVG/canvas-rendered nodes (circles, 40-56px) connected by animated edges (2px stroked paths with directional arrows). Typography: JetBrains Mono 500-700 for headings and data labels, Inter 400-500 for body. Color-coding follows algorithm visualization conventions: visited (emerald #10B981), queued/active (amber #F59E0B), unvisited (slate #334155), current pointer (cyan #06B6D4). Animated traversal effects. Dot-grid background at 0.04 opacity.

landingPageStyles.flow: The page is structured as a 3-step conversion funnel visualized as a graph traversal. You start at a 'source node' (the problem) and traverse through feature nodes to reach the 'destination node' (getting hired). A persistent graph visualization runs along the side/top showing your position in the funnel. Each step reveals a key feature.

sections.name: Source Node — The Problem
sections.description: A large graph visualization spans the full width. One node is highlighted cyan (YOU ARE HERE). Edges lead to 3 red 'problem' nodes: 'Scattered Resources', 'No Structure', 'No Feedback'. These nodes pulse red. Below the graph: a text section explaining the interview prep problem. Stats (1M+ engineers, 1000+ problems) appear as node labels in the graph. Company logos are placed as 'destination nodes' on the far right of the graph — Google, Meta, Amazon etc. are the goal nodes, currently unreachable (grayed out). The visual message: you need to traverse from here to there.

sections.name: Traversal Step 1 — Structured Learning (Courses + Video)
sections.description: The graph animates: your node traverses to the first green 'solution' node. A BFS ripple emanates. The section reveals COURSES as a tree/graph: category nodes (DSA, System Design, etc.) branch into course nodes with difficulty colors. Each course node is clickable and expands to show details + a video thumbnail. A LIVE VIDEO PLAYER is embedded — showing a NeetCode lesson clip with chapter navigation. The video frame is styled as a graph node that's been 'expanded'. Course thumbnails are the actual downloaded images placed inside node circles.

sections.name: Traversal Step 2 — Interactive Practice (Walkthroughs + NeetBot)
sections.description: Graph animates again: you traverse to the second solution node. Section reveals the INTERACTIVE WALKTHROUGH — a full embedded algorithm stepper. Shows 'Contains Duplicate' with array visualization, pointer, hash set building up, step controls. The stepper is styled with the graph node aesthetic (data inside node-like containers, edges connecting data flow). Next to it: NEETBOT AI section. A chat interface where the graph visualization continues — NeetBot is a special node connected to all problem nodes. The chat shows: User → 'stuck on two sum' → NeetBot → 'Use a hash map for O(1) lookups...' with a code snippet. NeetBot responses include mini graph/array visualizations inline.

sections.name: Destination Reached — Social Proof + CTA
sections.description: Final graph traversal: your node reaches the destination cluster. The previously grayed-out company nodes light up green one by one. Testimonials appear as 'completed traversal' cards — each person's path from start to their company node is drawn as a highlighted path in a mini graph. CTA section: the graph shows two paths from your current node — 'Free' (shorter, goes through NeetCode 150) and 'Pro' (full path, goes through all resources). Both lead to the destination. Large CTA buttons styled as graph nodes with pulsing edges. Practice tracker shown as a progress bar overlaid on a linked list visualization. Founder section: Navi's journey drawn as a literal graph — nodes for each career step, edges with timestamps.

landingPageStyles.animations: Graph traversal animations (nodes light up in BFS order, edges animate with stroke-dashoffset). Node hover shows tooltip with details. Each section transition triggers a graph traversal animation. Interactive stepper has smooth node-state transitions. Parallax on the background dot-grid. Staggered entrance for node clusters (30ms delay per node). Edge arrows animate directionally.
landingPageStyles.uniqueElement: A persistent graph visualization at the top of the page shows the user's journey through the funnel as an actual graph traversal. As they scroll, their 'current node' moves forward. The algorithm walkthrough is embedded and fully functional — users solve a problem right on the page. NeetBot responses include inline DSA visualizations.

variants.name: Neo Brutalism
variants.generalStyle: Light cream base (#FFFDF5) with bold black borders (3-4px), hard offset shadows (4-6px, no blur, solid black), sharp corners (border-radius: 0). Typography: Space Grotesk 700-900 for headings (uppercase, tight tracking -0.02em), DM Sans 400-500 for body. High-saturation accent blocks (hot red, vivid yellow, electric blue). Slightly rotated elements (-1 to 2deg) for playful energy. No gradients, no blur. Cards feel like stacked paper cutouts. Press interactions shift elements by shadow offset.

landingPageStyles.flow: The page leads with confrontation — 'Why are you still using LeetCode alone?' — then immediately proves NeetCode's advantage through a bold comparison, feature bento blocks, and an in-your-face product demo. No gentle funnel. This is Neo Brutalist: direct, unapologetic, high-energy. Every section has a strong opinion.

sections.name: Confrontation Hero
sections.description: Massive uppercase heading (Space Grotesk 900, 72-96px): 'STOP GRINDING BLINDLY.' with 'BLINDLY' in a hot-red highlight box with offset shadow. Below: a single-line subhead: 'NeetCode gives you structure, explanations, and an AI tutor.' Two CTA buttons: 'START FREE' (yellow background, black text, offset shadow, shifts on press) and 'GET PRO' (red background, white text). No hero image — just raw bold text. Company logos below in a thick-bordered strip: 'TRUSTED BY ENGINEERS AT:' followed by logo row on cream background.

sections.name: Comparison Smackdown
sections.description: A bold comparison table: 'NeetCode vs. Going It Alone'. Two columns with thick black borders. NeetCode column has a yellow header, 'alone' column has gray. Rows: 'Structured Roadmap' (✓ green vs ✗ red), 'Video Solutions for Every Problem' (✓ vs ✗), 'Interactive Step-by-Step Walkthroughs' (✓ vs ✗), 'AI Tutor (NeetBot)' (✓ vs ✗), 'Progress Tracking' (✓ vs ✗). NeetCode column has checkmarks in green blocks, 'alone' has X marks in red blocks. The table itself has a 4px black border and 6px offset shadow. Each ✓ row for NeetCode subtly links to the feature demo below.

sections.name: Feature Bento (3 Big Blocks)
sections.description: Three large stacked blocks, each with a colored header bar and thick border: BLOCK 1 (BLUE header) — 'INTERACTIVE WALKTHROUGHS': A live embedded algorithm stepper. The array [1,2,3,3] is rendered in bold bordered boxes. Pointer is a thick red arrow. Step controls are large brutalist buttons: '◀ PREV' 'NEXT ▶' 'RESET'. Hash set state shown in stacked boxes. The whole thing has a 4px black border and yellow background accent. BLOCK 2 (RED header) — 'VIDEO SOLUTIONS': Large video thumbnail with a play button (black triangle in a yellow circle). Below: course list with bold text, duration in bordered pills, difficulty as colored block labels. '1000+ explanations, every single problem.' BLOCK 3 (YELLOW header) — 'NEETBOT AI TUTOR': Chat interface with brutalist styling — thick bordered chat bubbles, no rounded corners. User message in white block, NeetBot response in blue block. Shows: 'I dont understand sliding window' → 'Think of it as maintaining a valid range by expanding right and shrinking left...' with a code snippet in a monospace bordered block. 'ASK NEETBOT →' CTA button.

sections.name: Testimonial Stack + Stats
sections.description: Testimonials as stacked paper cards with offset shadows and slight rotation. Each card has a bold company name header (colored block), photo, quote, and name. Stats shown as giant numbers in colored blocks: '1M+' in a yellow block, '1,000+' in a blue block, '150' in a red block (for NeetCode 150). The blocks are rotated 1-2 degrees for that brutalist energy.

sections.name: Direct CTA + Founder
sections.description: Large yellow background section: 'READY?' in 96px uppercase. Below: NeetCode 150 progress tracker in a thick-bordered frame — progress bar as a bold green-on-black bar, topic list as a bordered directory. Two massive CTA buttons side by side with offset shadows. Founder in a small bordered sidebar: portrait in a bordered square (not circle), 'Built by Navi. Google. Amazon. Capital One.' in blunt one-liner format. Footer: thick top border, blocky minimal layout, links as uppercase text.

landingPageStyles.animations: Minimal — brutalism means instant. Button press shifts position by shadow offset amount (transform: translate(4px, 4px), shadow disappears). Hover states: background color swap (instant, no transition). Comparison table rows highlight on hover with yellow wash. Feature blocks slide in from alternating sides (left/right) on scroll but with instant snap (no easing). Interactive elements (stepper, chat) respond instantly — no smooth state transitions.
landingPageStyles.uniqueElement: The comparison table is the hook — it immediately shows the value of NeetCode's hidden features (walkthroughs, video solutions, NeetBot) vs grinding alone. Each comparison row links down to the live feature demo. The confrontational tone ('STOP GRINDING BLINDLY') and bold typography create urgency. The interactive walkthrough and NeetBot chat are fully functional on the page.
